decision.observed_event: Their pallor and fangs are theatrical. They are posing as vampires.

appraisal.label: concern
appraisal.cause: A self-declared cousin sniffs out the act.

improv_read.player_bid: Vesna smells the dealer and reads what drives him.
improv_read.connection: Uktarl runs the act to extort coin without risk; a real vampire is risk, so he stalls.
improv_read.kit_choice: Kit answers the Insight with why they pose, not only how, and keeps the NPC in his part.

public_brief.objective: Keep the act standing in front of someone who may be the real thing.
public_brief.tactic: Deflect the question with courtly evasion and steer back to the toll.
public_brief.visible_cue: A muscle jumps in his jaw while his smile holds.
public_brief.player_opening: She can press him, play along, call the bluff, or pay.
public_brief.reply_to: You smell of tallow and sweat. Which nest turned you?
public_brief.kit_focus: Give the read as motive, coin and fear, then let the dealer try to hold the act anyway.
public_brief.mirror: steady energy, standard, dry humor: a cold read, then a slippery answer

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Up close, you read him plainly. The whole court is a costume worn for coin: the pallor and fangs are there to make strangers frightened enough to pay. And your word, cousins, has rattled him, because the last thing a man in painted fangs wants at his table is the real thing.

segments.speaker: Dealer
segments.text: Tallow keeps the candles lit, cousin, and sweat is what a long night at cards costs anyone, living or otherwise. As for the nest, we do not name our sires to strangers on the stair. Even kin must earn that. Ten gold for the road, and perhaps afterward we talk of old blood.

segments.speaker: Kit
segments.text: He hasn't answered the question. What now?
segments.reacts_to: we do not name our sires
